question: Trace a request inside a Sinatra application instance, from the method the middleware stack invokes to the route block's return value ending up as the response status and body: which methods run in between, and how is the matching route chosen when both the app and its parent class define routes?
reference: `Base#call` dups the app and runs `call!`, which wraps `dispatch!` in `invoke` (catching `:halt`); `dispatch!` merges request params and runs static files and before filters, then `route!` walks the routes for the request method on the class and then its superclasses, `process_route` matches the compiled Mustermann pattern and conditions and merges path params, and `route_eval` throws `:halt` with the block's value, which `invoke` turns into status and body (lib/sinatra/base.rb).

read.note: call dups the instance; call! wraps dispatch! in invoke and finishes the response
route! walks routes then superclass routes; route_eval throws :halt; process_route matches pattern, conditions and merges params
invoke turns the halted value into status/body; dispatch! runs static!, before filters and route!

question: When a route block raises an exception, trace how it turns into the response the client receives: where is it caught, how is the status code decided, and how is a handler that the app registered for that exception class (or one of its ancestors) or for a status code found and run?
reference: `dispatch!` rescues the exception and calls `handle_exception!`, which stores it in `sinatra.error`, takes the status from `http_status` (Sinatra::Error subclasses such as NotFound and BadRequest) or 500, and asks `error_block!` for a handler registered with `error`: it looks up the exception class (walking the app's superclasses and then the exception's superclasses) and then the status code, running each handler through `process_route` (lib/sinatra/base.rb).

read.note: Sinatra::Error, BadRequest and NotFound define http_status
dispatch! rescues into handle_exception!; status from http_status; error_block! looks up handlers by class, superclass and status
error registers handlers via compile! into @errors keyed by class or code

question: When a route calls `erb :index`, trace how the template file is found on disk, compiled, cached between renders and wrapped in a layout, including what happens when no layout file exists.
reference: `erb` calls the private `render`, which merges engine options from settings and calls `compile_template`; for a Symbol it fetches from the instance's `TemplateCache` (cleared per request when reload_templates is on), uses an inline/named template if defined, otherwise `find_template` yields `views/index.<ext>` candidates for the extensions `Tilt` maps to the engine; after rendering, `render` recurses for the layout, and a missing layout file throws `:layout_missing`, which `render` catches to return the bare output (lib/sinatra/base.rb).

question: Trace a GET request for a file that exists in the app's public folder: where is the file detected, how is it sent, which settings shape the response headers, and which parts of normal request processing are skipped?
reference: In `dispatch!`, `static!` runs first for GET/HEAD when the `static` setting is on: it resolves the path under `public_folder`, rejects paths escaping it, sets `env['sinatra.static_file']`, applies `static_cache_control` and `static_headers`, and calls `send_file`, which serves the file through `Rack::Files#serving` and halts, so before filters and routes never run, and `dispatch!` skips after filters because `sinatra.static_file` is set (lib/sinatra/base.rb).

question: Which Rack middleware sits in front of a Sinatra app's own request handling, how is that chain assembled when the app is instantiated, and where do middlewares the app adds itself end up relative to the built-in ones?
reference: `Base.new` wraps the instance with `build`, which creates a `Rack::Builder`, calls `setup_default_middleware` (`ExtendedRack`, `ShowExceptions` when show_exceptions is on, `Rack::MethodOverride`, `Rack::Head`, logging, sessions, `Rack::Protection` and its HostAuthorization) and then `setup_middleware` (the `use` entries of the class and its superclasses, after the built-ins), runs the instance last and returns a `Wrapper`; `use` clears the cached `prototype` so the chain is rebuilt (lib/sinatra/base.rb).

question: How are before and after filters organised: where does a filter declaration get stored, how are filters inherited from a parent application class run and in what order, and how does a filter declared for a path pattern decide whether it applies to a request?
reference: `before` and `after` call `add_filter`, which stores `compile!(type, path, block)` (a Mustermann pattern, the pending conditions and a wrapper; default path /.*/) in the class's `filters[type]`; `filter!` first recurses into the superclass and then runs the class's own filters, each through `process_route`, which calls the block only when the path pattern and conditions match; `dispatch!` runs before filters ahead of `route!` and after filters in its ensure block (lib/sinatra/base.rb).

read.note: filter! runs superclass filters first, each via process_route
reset! gives each class its own filters hash
before/after -> add_filter -> filters[type] << compile!
compile! builds Mustermann pattern, conditions, wrapper
dispatch! runs before filters before route!, after filters in ensure

question: How is the classic style (a script that requires 'sinatra' and defines routes at the top level) wired onto the modular core: which class receives the top-level calls, how do they get there, which defaults differ from a plain subclass of the base class, and what starts the web server when the script ends?
reference: lib/sinatra/main.rb sets `Sinatra::Application`'s app_file and run setting (and command-line options), extends the top-level object with `Delegator`, which forwards `get`, `set`, `use` and the other DSL methods to `Delegator.target` (Application), and registers `at_exit { Application.run! }`; `Application < Base` in lib/sinatra/base.rb turns on logging, method_override and run, and `run!` picks a Rackup handler and calls `start_server`.

question: How is content negotiation organised: which classes model the entries of a request's Accept header and the media types a route offers, how are the header's entries ranked, and how does a route limited to certain formats both match a request and set the response content type?
reference: `Request#accept` parses the Accept header into `AcceptEntry` objects sorted by their priority (q value, wildcards, parameter count), and `preferred_type` returns the first offered type whose `MimeTypeEntry` accepts an entry; a route option such as `provides:` is turned by `compile!` into a call to the `provides` condition, which matches when the response type is already one of the offered types or `preferred_type` finds one, and then sets `content_type` (lib/sinatra/base.rb).
